sections.section_title: The Transfiguration: Glory on the Mountain
sections.summary: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John on a high mountain after six days, with Moses and Elijah appearing alongside him; the Father's voice from a bright cloud declares, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him,' and when the disciples look up they see Jesus only.

Coming down the mountain, Jesus commands secrecy until the resurrection, then identifies John the Baptist as the Elijah who has already come and was not recognized, drawing a parallel between the forerunner's fate and the Son of Man's coming suffering at the same hands.

sections.section_title: The Disciples' Failure and the Healing of the Boy
sections.summary: The disciples fail to heal a demon-possessed boy; Jesus rebukes the 'faithless and twisted generation,' heals the boy instantly, and tells the disciples their failure was due to their 'little faith,' declaring that even mustard-seed-sized genuine faith can accomplish the impossible.

Jesus predicts that the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, killed, and raised on the third day, and the disciples are greatly distressed, having focused on the death without hearing the resurrection.

sections.section_title: The Temple Tax: Sons and Strangers
sections.summary: Jesus teaches Peter that as sons of the King they are free from the temple tax, but instructs him to pay it to avoid causing offense, providing the payment miraculously through a coin in a fish's mouth, enacting the principle of voluntary self-limitation for others' sake.
